decision: Classify the event as OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE caused by an environment screenshot-pipeline failure. The responsive title and URL reads establish tab liveness, so the timeout does not establish page, game, or business-action failure. Only observation-scope handling is supported; no semantic business action is allowed without fresh reliable state evidence.
facts: The recorded incident contains repeated screenshot capture timeouts and a later busy rejection for a capture still completing after timeout.
Independent title and URL reads remained responsive on the affected tab.
No screenshot image was obtainable during the recorded failure window.
The failure artifact classifies the incident as ENVIRONMENT_TOOL_FAILURE and the screenshot contract represents capture timeout as OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE with scope OBSERVATION.
The screenshot contract sets is_game_failure to false and leaves pending_action_failed unset for observation failures.
The screenshot contract requires proof that the page is dead before advising a new capture surface; repeated capture failures on a live page do not satisfy that condition.
For the recorded pre-click occurrence, the decision control was never clicked and the week was not committed at that boundary.
inferences: The evidence is consistent with a hung backend per-tab screenshot task or transport stall while the page itself remained alive.
Because liveness was positively observed, automatic browser or game recovery is not supported by the caller-side recovery contract for this failure window.
A fresh trustworthy observation is required before any semantic state-dependent conclusion could be made.
unknowns: The page's visual and semantic state during the screenshot-unavailable interval is UNKNOWN.
The contents of the missing screenshot are UNKNOWN.
Whether or when the backend capture task would eventually complete is UNKNOWN.
The host backend's underlying implementation-level root cause is not directly established by the provided repository evidence.
reason: Tab liveness evidence narrows the failure to observation/capture scope, but it supplies no fresh semantic state and no authorization. A screenshot timeout cannot be converted into an action outcome or permission for a business action.
